name: Westside Gunn
sources: Ambrosia for Heads — Daringer on creating the Griselda sound (https://ambrosiaforheads.com/2022/09/producer-daringer-on-creating-griselda-sound/)
notes: Daringer's board described in two words the research quotes directly: "lean and dry". Lean is `kick.densityPerBar` 2–3 at `syncopation` 0.18, a `snare.ghost.prob` of 0.03 for the thin snare, and `hihat.continuous` false at 0.30 for "often no hats at all". Dry is `velocityTiers` topping at 102 and hat velocities at 0.42–0.62 — quiet, but harder-edged than Roc Marciano's, because these drums are placed rather than dissolved. The one thing this record adds that its neighbours do not is percussion: the research says the ad-libs "function as the percussion layer", so `percs` runs 1–3 hits a bar on `offbeat` placement while every other Griselda-adjacent entry here runs 0–1. Melodically it is a two-note motif rather than a phrase — `halfStepDissonance` 0.16, `intervals.leap` 0.28, `chordToneBias` 0.5, all the most dissonant settings in the batch — and the tracks are short (`sectionBars.outro` 2, intro 2–4, a hookless structure at weight 4). ⚠ **The research says "no fills" and this model has a fill cycle anyway.** `smallEveryBars` 4 / `bigEveryBars` 8 is a fixed authoring fingerprint across this batch, so the claim is carried instead by `snareRoll.gapProb` 0.60 (the fill is mostly holes), a low velocity ceiling, and `transitions.fillBeforeSection` false, which is the fill a listener would actually notice. If a listening pass wants it gone, raise `smallEveryBars` here first. ⚠ The `i–VII` and `i–ii` families are **INFERRED**; the research names a single sustained chord or a two-note motif and nothing else. ⚠ `confidence` is medium — the research rates the producer's gear and aesthetic medium-high, which documents a sound, not a session. ⚠ **The bass pool was widened after `bass.rs` measured it at 0.947 distinct against a floor of 0.95.** It was authored with NO passing tones, followRootsProb 0.96, anticipationProb 0.06 over register [22,40] — a faithful description of a sample-loop bass, and one that leaves a seed nothing to vary but root and octave. Now ["P5"], root lock 0.9, anticipation 0.18, register [22,44]. The line is still overwhelmingly root-on-kick; what changed is how many different records it can be, not how busy any one of them is. ⚠ The chord voicing moved up to [45, 87] so the bass stays under the harmony — it started at 38 against a bass reaching 44, an overlap of 7. The span is preserved; a voicing that low was competing with the bass rather than sitting over it. ⚠ **The countermelody reached only 961 distinct answers in 1000 seeds against a floor of 980**, so it was given range: densityRatio 0.45. A counter is combinatorial in the styles it may pick, its density against the melody, and the phrase length it answers inside — one style over a thin density inside a single phrase length has almost nothing a seed can vary. ⚠ **The 1-bar phrase length was removed** (was [1,2], now [2,4]). A one-bar phrase looped four times carries less entropy than a four-bar phrase, and it is the countermelody it strangles hardest: a counter answers *inside* the melody’s phrase, so a one-bar shape leaves it nowhere to go. Every worst offender on `counter.rs` carried it. ⛔ The previous session recorded this exact mistake and it arrived again from the other direction — distinctness is combinatorial in the shape LENGTH, not in the option count.
